close_reason: Added two tests: alert_trigger_unknown_dispatch_on_hostile_input probes 10 hostile JSON shapes (null, [], 42, 'hello', true, {} without @type, @type:42, @type:null, @type:[], unknown tag) and asserts all dispatch into Unknown(Value) with the original input preserved bit-exactly. alert_trigger_unknown_round_trips_through_serialize confirms Unknown round-trips through serialize→deserialize. This also closes the review's least-confident flag (the 15% uncertainty about whether non-object inputs gracefully fall into Unknown without panic) — now verified by probe.
description:
src/lib.rs:589-612 implements Deserialize for AlertTrigger by deserializing to serde_json::Value, then dispatching on the @type field via v.get("@type").and_then(|t| t.as_str()).unwrap_or("").

Edge cases that are not covered by any existing test:

1. trigger = [1, 2, 3] — array, not object. v.get("@type") returns None → unwrap_or("") → falls into AlertTrigger::Unknown(Value::Array(...)). Re-serializes as the original array. Spec-compliant (preserve), but no test asserts this.

2. trigger = "some string" — string, not object. v.get("@type") on a Value::String returns None → Unknown(Value::String(...)). Same preservation behavior, no test.

3. trigger = {"@type": 42, "foo": "bar"} — non-string @type. as_str() returns None → unwrap_or("") → Unknown(v). Preserves the original object with the numeric @type. No test.

4. trigger = null — Value::Null. Same path → Unknown(Value::Null). Re-serialization writes null back. Spec interaction: an Alert with trigger:null is malformed per RFC 8984 §4.5.2 (trigger is mandatory). The crate's policy is preserve-not-validate, so this is consistent, but no test.

These are not bugs — the implementation handles them all via the Unknown variant per the spec MUST-preserve rule. But the absence of explicit tests means a future refactor (e.g. switching to a serde_json::Map intermediate, or adding stricter validation) could silently break round-trip behavior on hostile or malformed input without any test signaling the regression.

Add four round-trip tests, one per case above, asserting:
- deserialize succeeds and yields AlertTrigger::Unknown(_)
- re-serialize produces byte-equivalent JSON to the input

These give a tripwire for any future change to the manual Deserialize implementation.
title: AlertTrigger custom Deserialize lacks tests for non-object input and non-string @type
